rule.description: Members of the per-quality media source descriptor (address, quality, format, width, height, bitrate) cross a boundary as loose unrelated values, or are stored at rest as parallel primitive column arrays, instead of being carried together by one descriptor structure.

detection_threshold: >= 3 distinct descriptor members at one parameter list / JSX attribute list / type declaration

checks.description: Detect a transfer boundary (function/constructor parameter list, or JSX attribute list) that hands three or more distinct descriptor members across as loose unrelated values.
checks.detected_relation: boundary -> scattered descriptor members as loose values
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The values belong to one playlist entry; passing them as unrelated peers forces every caller and callee to restate the grouping and alignment by convention, which is the data-clump relation this case targets.

matches.evidence: render hands the currently selected quality plus five parallel column arrays (addresses, quality axis, widths, heights, bitrates) to the wrapped video component as separate attributes.
The context-injecting wrapper peels the five columns off the context value and forwards them (plus format and the selected quality) to the video core as unrelated attributes.
The master-playlist builder accepts addresses, bitrates, widths and heights as four loose defaulted positional parameters and re-zips them into per-entry records by index inside its body.

checks.description: Detect a type alias or interface that stores three or more distinct descriptor members as parallel arrays of primitive scalars (the at-rest column layout that the loose handoffs feed from).
checks.detected_relation: type declaration -> descriptor members as parallel value columns
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Declaring the members as unrelated peer arrays erases the record they came from; every producer and consumer downstream must keep the columns aligned by index, and adding a per-quality field means declaring yet another column instead of extending one record.

matches.evidence: The video core's internal prop type declares the address column as a string array and width/height/bitrate columns as number arrays alongside the selected quality; the quality-axis column uses the shared Quality type so its array-of-primitive form is not required for detection.
The video-source context value exposes addresses, widths, heights and bitrates as four peer arrays (plus the quality-axis column), distributed wholesale to every context consumer.
The built-in native component's prop type accepts the five columns as separate string/number arrays even though the component uses none of their content.
The built-in MP4/MSE plugin component's prop type accepts the five columns as separate string/number arrays; the class body never reads them.

The built-in HLS component's prop type accepts the five columns as separate string/number arrays and resolves quality switches by index against them; the module-local record type that used to describe one entry was deleted.

excluded: Destructured (ObjectPattern) parameters, rest parameters and JSX spread attributes: values arrive bundled there, so the boundary is not the scatter being targeted; equivalent bundling is an accepted repair shape.
Type members whose value type is not a primitive-scalar array (records such as PlaySource[]/Source[], scalars, unions and maps): bundled or single-member shapes are not the parallel-column layout.
'src'/'source'/'play_url'-only identifiers: a bare address name alone carries no grouping signal and is deliberately outside the vocabulary.
JSX call-like expressions and function call sites: transfer is attributed to the definition side (parameter list / attribute list), not to every invocation.
Test sources (__tests__ directories, *.spec.ts(x), *.d.ts) and every file outside packages/*/src: the rule covers production pipeline code only.
